answer: I would anchor trust in Timestamped commit chain with no gaps. With a commit every day for ninety days, no gaps, a single basalt check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that a commit every day for ninety days, no gaps — so privacy survives, and the mesa is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The lantern grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
